title: Problem-Solving & Data Analysis
description: About 15% of SAT Math. Ratios, rates and units, percentages, one- and two-variable data, probability, and what a study can and cannot conclude.
goals: Convert units and set up rates without losing track of what is "per" what
Find percent change from the right base, and chain percent changes by multiplying
Read a scatterplot and its line of best fit; interpret slope and intercept
Find conditional probabilities from a two-way table
Tell apart random sampling (generalize) and random assignment (cause and effect)

scaffold.title: Percents, rates and data
scaffold.content: These questions are short on algebra and long on reading. Most misses come from the base of a percent, a unit left unconverted, or the wrong denominator in a two-way table.
keyPoints: Successive changes multiply: up 20% then down 20% is 1.2 × 0.8 = 0.96
"Given" in a probability names the denominator: P(A given B) = count(A and B) ÷ count(B)
Random sample → generalize to the population; random assignment → cause and effect

examples.problem: A price rose from $160 to $200. By what percent did it increase?
examples.solution: (200 − 160) ÷ 160 = 40/160 = 25%. Dividing by 200 (the new price) gives 20%, the classic trap.

examples.problem: Of 30 students who own a bike, 18 ride to school. If one bike owner is chosen at random, what is the probability they ride to school?
examples.solution: The condition "owns a bike" makes 30 the denominator: 18/30 = 3/5.

problems.problem: A car travels 60 miles per hour. How far does it go in 2.5 hours?
A $80 jacket is 15% off. What is the sale price?

problems.problem: A machine fills 45 bottles in 3 minutes. At this rate, how many bottles does it fill in 8 minutes?
After a 50% increase, a price is $120. What was the original price?
A line of best fit is y = 3x + 2. What does it predict when x = 5?
